In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bloch-Nordsiek formula for the one loop thermal corrections in the case of a hard external particle scattering in a heat bath is valid in all cases.
the Bloch-Nordsiecki thermometry is not a reliable method to measure temperature of the QFT heat bath.
, at one-loop order, the leading infra-red divergence is not a logarithmic one, but is instead a power divergence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermal corrections to the hard process are not simply the thermal corrections to a T = 0 process, but rather a combination of the thermal and the non-thermal effects.

the thermal distribution of the 3-momentum of the hard particles in the rest frame of the heat bath has a thermal width which is of the order of log(Q/T), where the log(Q/T) term is a result of the resummation of thermal photon emissions and absorption.
the leading thermal corrections to hard scattering are of the same order as those at zero temperature and can not be neglected.
